title: Declared repo facts
description: A consumer's `.claude/ops-repo-meta.json`: the facts about a repo that CANNOT be detected and have no other owner. Read by the framework-default `ops-repo-meta`, and by `route-event.sh` at the edge to resolve a cross-repo target. Written by `ops-install`. This is NOT the retired `ai-ops.yml` in JSON — it is a strict subset. Everything that file also held has exactly one owner elsewhere now: branch model, base, release base and merge strategy are private to `ops-branching`; the CI provider is internal to `ops-ci`; skill pointers are gone because a capability is found by its name. `additionalProperties: false` at every level is deliberate, so an attempt to put any of that back fails loudly instead of drifting. Every key is optional except `version`: a single-repo project on one line needs no file at all.

version.description: The file's shape. Bump only on a breaking change to it.

topology.description: Which repo fills each role. The rule is: declare the roles that are NOT the repo this file lives in, and any role left out resolves to this repo. So a single-repo project omits the block entirely; a code repo whose issues live elsewhere declares `issues`; and the issues repo declares `code`, which is the ONLY place the code repo can be named — detection there would read the issues repo's own remote.

code.description: Where the code lives, when this file is NOT in the code repo. On the code repo itself, omit it: detection reads it from the git remote and a stale hand-written copy would be worse. On the issues repo of a split topology this is required, because it is the only way the edge router can learn which repo the routine should work in.

issues.description: Where the backlog lives, when it is a different repo from the code. Nothing in a code repo points at its issues repo, which is the main reason this file exists.

releases.description: Where publication happens, if not the code repo.

learnings.description: Where proto-learning issues are filed. NOT automatically the issues repo: where issues are public and code is not, a proto-learning is an internal note and belongs with the code — which is what omitting this gives you.

lines.description: The version lines currently taking work. Omit the whole block for a repo with no version lines: the default is a single line and the default branch is the whole story. Declare it as a set, because a repo with several live lines has several legitimate bases and the wrong-base gate tests membership, not equality.

live.description: Every line taking work now. Detection can list `vN/*` branches but cannot know which lines are still worked — a line may exist and be finished, or exist only as a `main` taking security fixes.

primary.description: The line work starts on before being ported. MUST be a member of `live` — a cross-field rule JSON Schema cannot express, enforced by validate-repo-meta.sh. Not necessarily the newest line, and not necessarily the default branch.

port_order.description: `upward` = primary is older, ports go to newer lines. `downward` = the reverse. A human decision; the engine never infers it.

labels.description: Label overrides, keyed by PURPOSE and not by name — which is what lets a repo rename a label without touching a loop. Partial: name only what you are changing, and the `ops/`-namespaced framework defaults fill in the rest. Point a key at a label the repo already has rather than creating a second one that means the same thing.

ready.description: Default `ops/ready-for-ai`. The only gate the issue loop acts on.

land.description: Default `ops/auto-merge`. The human approval for landing.

triaged.description: Default `ops/triaged`. Written by triage, never a trigger.

line.description: A line name, e.g. `v17`. The line is the NAME, not a branch: which of its branches exist is `ops-branching`'s private business, and a line may legitimately have only a `main`.

label.description: A GitHub label name. New labels SHOULD be namespaced `ops/`, but this is not enforced: an override often points at a label the repo had before the engine arrived, and that name is not ours to dictate.
